name: Marketing / Strategic Communication
hook: Students generate ten campaigns in an hour, then have to defend why nine of them are bad.

make.body: Physical packaging or a point-of-sale piece for a real local client. Holding a mockup surfaces every decision a slide deck hides: size, weight, what the customer reads first from arm’s length.

build.body: A message-testing harness. Students generate a wide spread of positioning variants, then build a simple landing page per variant and measure. The AI supplies volume; the student supplies the judgment about which variant is worth defending.

plan.txt: Land one real client, even a campus organization. Written brief, signed by the client.
Generate wide with AI in class, then cut down to three positions with a written rationale per cut. Submit packaging cut file.
Build one page per position, run whatever traffic is available for five days.
Client presentation with the physical mockup and the actual numbers. The client picks. Students debrief the gap between their favorite and the client’s.

prompt: Generate twelve distinct positioning statements for this product, aimed at this audience: [describe product and audience]. Make them genuinely different from each other in strategy, not in wording: vary what need is being claimed, what the competition is, and what the customer has to believe. Number them. Then for each one, write the single sentence a skeptical customer would say to reject it.
